Seed.//: Creates demo accounts, projects and tasks. Must stay false in production: the seed data includes an Admin whose password is committed to this repository.

Reminders.//: Reminders people set on tasks and events, plus the automatic 'due soon' notice for tasks. IntervalSeconds is how often due reminders are looked for (a reminder is at most that late). WindowHours is how far ahead of the due date the 'due soon' notice is sent.

Notifications.//: EmailEnabled sends an email for the important notifications (task assigned, invitation, reminder, mention) to users who left email notifications on. Off by default: on a mail plan with a daily limit these emails use the same quota as sign-in codes.

WeeklySummary.//: The weekly summary email for users who switched it on. Sent on Day at Hour (0-23) in each user's own time zone; needs a mail provider (EmailSettings).

Push.//: Web Push: notifications to browsers that are not showing the app. PublicKey / PrivateKey are a VAPID key pair (generate once, keep the private key secret); empty switches device notifications off. Subject is a mailto: or https: address the push services can contact.
Push.Subject: mailto:support@miqat.app

Calls.//: Voice and video calls go directly between the two browsers. IceServers are the helpers they use to find each other: the public STUN server below is enough on most home and office networks. People on strict networks also need a relay (TURN): either add an entry with urls / username / credential to IceServers, or point Turn at a coturn server run with use-auth-secret (Urls + Secret; each user then gets a password that works for TtlSeconds). The easiest relay is a hosted one with a free plan: put its address for ICE servers in Relay:Url, and its key in Relay:Token when the service wants the key as a Bearer token (Cloudflare: https://rtc.live.cloudflare.com/v1/turn/keys/<key id>/credentials/generate-ice-servers plus the API token). Leave Token empty when the key is part of the address (Metered: https://<app>.metered.live/api/v1/turn/credentials?apiKey=<key>). Set them as environment values, never in this file.

LoggingNotes: EF Core logs every executed statement at Information. Useful locally, a liability in production: it multiplies log volume, costs time per request, and writes column names like PasswordHash into the log stream — hence the Warning overrides below.
